entries.update: Hillary Clinton was deposed by the Republican-led House Oversight Committee on February 26 as part of an Epstein investigation, with Bill Clinton scheduled for deposition on February 27.

Hillary Clinton and Bill Clinton testified in closed-door sessions before the House Oversight Committee as part of its Epstein investigation, with Hillary Clinton stating she did not know Jeffrey Epstein and Bill Clinton testifying the day after. Neither has been accused of crimes related to Epstein.
The House Oversight Committee released video depositions of Bill and Hillary Clinton on Monday as part of its Jeffrey Epstein investigation. The depositions took place the week before their release.
The House Oversight Committee voted on a bipartisan basis to subpoena Attorney General Pam Bondi regarding the DOJ's handling of Jeffrey Epstein-related files.
The House Oversight Committee voted on a bipartisan basis to subpoena Attorney General Pam Bondi regarding the DOJ's handling of Jeffrey Epstein-related files.
The DOJ released previously withheld documents from the Epstein files, including FBI interview reports relating to allegations made against President Donald Trump by a woman.

Rep. James Comer and the House Oversight Committee are investigating the Epstein case. The federal government requested that New Mexico stop its investigation into Epstein's Zorro Ranch around 2019 during Trump's first term.
Richard Kahn, Jeffrey Epstein's accountant, testified before the House Oversight Committee; Epstein accumulated hundreds of millions of dollars over his career.

Tova Noel, a former prison guard at the Metropolitan Correctional Center who was on duty the night Jeffrey Epstein died, is scheduled to testify before the House Oversight Committee as part of an ongoing congressional investigation.

New documents are revealing Jeffrey Epstein's network of connections and relationships cultivated among powerful and elite circles in the original sex-trafficking investigation that originated in Florida.
Leon Black and his wife Debra purchased the property at 1111 Calle Vista Drive in Beverly Hills for $38 million in 2016, which was subsequently sold for $47 million.

Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche dismissed suggestions that victims of convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein have been ignored by the Justice Department and defended the Trump administration's handling of the investigation.
Metropolitan Police chief Mark Rowley stated police are investigating whether an email from Mandelson to Epstein constitutes a criminal offence.

Democrats walked out of a House Oversight Committee briefing with Attorney General Pam Bondi regarding Epstein files; GOP Chairman James Comer characterized the walkout as premeditated, and Bondi stated she would 'follow the law' in response.
Wall Street titan Leon Black paid Jeffrey Epstein $170 million, which Black described as compensation for tax and estate work.
Leon Black paid Jeffrey Epstein $170 million, which Black described as payment for tax and estate work.
David A. Ross sought Jeffrey Epstein's help to build art museums and is now facing fallout related to that association.
Jeffrey Epstein's accountant Richard Khan and lawyer Darren Indyke testified before the House Oversight Committee, both stating the DOJ never interviewed them about Epstein's crimes.
Epstein survivors filed a class action lawsuit against the Trump administration and Google seeking at least $1,000 per survivor and court-ordered removal of their personal information by Google.
A man was interviewed on suspicion of sex trafficking in connection with the Al Fayed investigation, following earlier interviews with three women under caution.
Ramsey Elkholy introduced Jeffrey Epstein to women as young as 18 years old over nearly a decade, with correspondence documented in emails between them.
Jeffrey Epstein provided funding to scientists, and the lack of legal or public scrutiny in science philanthropy allowed him to cultivate relationships with scientists.
Epstein files indicate a 15-year-old girl met then-Prince Andrew at Buckingham Palace. Mandelson attempted to get access to 10 Downing Street for Epstein's goddaughter.
Attorney General Pam Bondi was fired by President Trump on Thursday; her handling of Epstein files was a point of congressional interest.
The Epstein files were released containing accusations against rich and powerful people, but the DOJ made no additional arrests, with legal experts citing lack of evidence.
Todd Blanche assumed the role of Interim Attorney General on Thursday, replacing Pam Bondi, and stated he wants to distance the Department of Justice from its work on Epstein files.

Virginia Giuffre, prior to her death, accused Jeffrey Epstein of trafficking her to Prince Andrew, brother of King Charles. The Giuffre family is urging King Charles to meet with Epstein survivors in the United States.
Jeffrey Epstein spent his final days of freedom in Paris, where he met with influential figures.
According to an FBI interview, Epstein had sex in a vehicle in a prison parking lot while on work release from a Florida jail approximately 20 years ago.

Bill Gates has agreed to appear before the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform in June as part of its investigation into deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is also scheduled to testify before the same House panel as part of the Epstein probe.

Attorney General Pam Bondi did not appear for a House Oversight Committee deposition subpoenaed in connection with its investigation into the Jeffrey Epstein files. The DOJ communicated that Bondi would not appear and informed the committee that its subpoena is essentially moot, though committee members maintain the subpoena remains valid.

The Department of Justice announced that Attorney General Pam Bondi would not testify before the House Oversight Committee, at least temporarily, despite having been subpoenaed as part of the committee's probe into the Jeffrey Epstein files. Separately, UK politician Peter Mandelson was reported to have attempted to obtain access to 10 Downing Street for a person described as Epstein's 'goddaughter.'

Melania Trump delivered a televised statement from the White House denying any connection to Jeffrey Epstein, stating 'I have never had any knowledge of Epstein's abuse of his victims,' 'I was never involved in any capacity,' 'I've never been friends with Epstein,' and 'I am not Epstein's victim.' She called on Congress to continue the investigation and hold hearings focused on Epstein's survivors, and declared that claims linking her to Epstein 'need to end today.'

On April 9, 2026, Melania Trump issued a rare public statement denying that Jeffrey Epstein introduced her to Donald Trump and calling on Congress to hold a hearing for Epstein survivors. Former Justice Department chief Pam Bondi refused to appear before a congressional Epstein hearing, with a subpoena for her testimony remaining in effect and Democrats criticizing her absence. Rep. Thomas Massie argued that bringing survivors back before Congress would be redundant and that the duty to act rests with federal prosecutors.

Melania Trump issued a rare public statement on Thursday denying any ties to Jeffrey Epstein, calling him 'disgraceful.' The statement was described as unexpected given her typically low public profile, and her adviser spoke publicly about what motivated her to issue it.

Melania Trump made a surprise public statement calling for testimony from Jeffrey Epstein victims. House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer, a Republican from Kentucky, responded to her statement and confirmed that congressional hearings featuring Epstein victims will take place. Separately, Epstein survivors pushed back on the call for public testimony. The House Oversight Committee has been investigating allegations of sex trafficking connected to Epstein, who was a convicted sex offender and is deceased.

A federal judge dismissed Donald Trump's defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal, which had centered on the outlet's reporting about a letter allegedly connected to Jeffrey Epstein's 50th birthday. The judge ruled that Trump failed to sufficiently allege 'actual malice,' the legal standard required for public figures in defamation cases.

The Justice Department's Office of Inspector General announced a review of the DOJ's compliance with laws requiring the release of Epstein-related records, amid concerns that required documents have not been fully disclosed.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick appeared before the House Oversight Committee on Wednesday in connection with the Epstein investigation. Ahead of the hearing, Committee Chair James Comer told reporters that Lutnick was not '100% truthful' about visiting Epstein's island.

A federal judge ordered the release of a document purported to be a suicide note attributed to Jeffrey Epstein, with the unsealing occurring on a Wednesday following a request by The New York Times. The note's authenticity has not been fully verified. Lutnick's testimony before the House Oversight Committee was conducted as a closed-door session.

Former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene claimed on CBS News that President Trump is targeting Republicans who voted to release Epstein files, citing Rep. Thomas Massie's primary defeat as an example. Separately, a trespasser who illegally accessed Epstein's private island Little St. James claimed he was hog-tied and held in a dungeon on the property.

British police issued a public appeal for witnesses on a Friday as part of an investigation into potential sexual misconduct offenses by former Prince Andrew, with the probe connected to Jeffrey Epstein. Newly released papers revealed Prince Andrew was coached on how to justify his qualifications for a UK trade ambassador role after lawmakers accused him of prioritizing his Epstein ties over British interests. Sarah Kellen, described as both an alleged survivor and recruiter for Epstein, testified in a closed-door session before lawmakers, reportedly naming three individuals tied to abuse. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick donated $5 million to House Republicans after agreeing to be interviewed by lawmakers about his relationship with Epstein, according to the New York Times.

FEC filings confirmed that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick donated the $5 million to the Congressional Leadership Fund, a House Republican super PAC, on April 1, specifically ahead of his congressional testimony regarding his ties to Jeffrey Epstein.

A U.S. document repository described as a 'library' has been established in New York to house 3.5 million pages of Epstein-related documents, aimed at providing accountability for victims, according to Al Jazeera. Rep. Thomas Massie attributed his primary loss to Trump-backed challenger Ed Gallrein to his bipartisan advocacy, particularly his push to release the Epstein files.

Rep. Thomas Massie, despite losing his primary race after being targeted by President Trump, promised to expose additional names from the Epstein files before his term ends in approximately seven months.

Pam Bondi appeared before the House Oversight Committee in a closed-door transcribed interview on Friday regarding the Epstein files, despite having been removed from her role as attorney general in April. A lawyer representing Epstein survivors told BBC News that his clients lack confidence in how UK police would treat them, casting doubt on their willingness to cooperate with the British inquiry into Prince Andrew.

During her closed-door testimony before the House Oversight Committee, Bondi refused to answer questions about President Trump's involvement in the Epstein files release and instead blamed Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel for issues with the release. Following the interview, House Democrats announced plans to seek subpoenas for both Blanche and Patel. Epstein survivor Danielle Besnky spoke out during the proceedings, stating she wants 'baseline humanity' from Bondi.

New Mexico lawmakers announced they will issue subpoenas to government and private institutions as the first major step in their state investigation into Jeffrey Epstein's activities in New Mexico, with the goal of determining whether additional prosecutions are warranted.
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and Rep. Madeleine Dean had a heated exchange during a House Appropriations Committee hearing over the state of the Jeffrey Epstein investigation.

The House Oversight Committee released transcripts of interviews related to the Epstein files on Thursday. Chairman James Comer separately requested the DOJ investigate allegations of sexual abuse by individuals in Jeffrey Epstein's orbit, based on claims made by a former Epstein assistant.

The House Oversight Committee released the transcript of Pam Bondi's closed-door interview, sparking a dispute between Republicans and Democrats over her claims, including her attribution of responsibility for the Epstein files release to then-Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche. Sen. Ron Wyden launched an inquiry into why billionaire Leon Black paid Jeffrey Epstein approximately $170 million for alleged tax planning services. The Committee called on the DOJ to investigate sexual misconduct allegations made by former Epstein assistant Sarah Kellen against two of Epstein's associates. A former correction officer testified before the Committee that she was not the orange shape seen moving up the stairs near Epstein's cell tier on the night of his death.
Former Epstein prison guard Tova Noel publicly addressed how conspiracy theories and threats have disrupted her life, including questions raised about her browsing history and bank transactions.
Nancy Mace is running for South Carolina governor while facing political headwinds including President Trump endorsing her opponent following her vote on the Epstein files.

An Epstein victim testified before U.S. Congress members that she had dinner at Prince Andrew's apartment in Buckingham Palace, marking the first time a woman abused and trafficked by Epstein has publicly spoken of attending royal residences.
Bill Gates has retained Jake Greenberg, former top investigative counsel to the House Oversight Committee, to advise him on testimony related to Jeffrey Epstein, according to the NY Times.
Epstein's personal assistant testified before Congress that she arranged calls between Epstein and President Trump, and reportedly provided lawmakers with 'a lot of names' during her testimony.

Bill Gates appeared voluntarily before the House Oversight Committee on Wednesday for a closed-door interview about his ties to Jeffrey Epstein, providing prepared opening remarks and stating he had no knowledge of Epstein's criminal conduct. Committee Chairman James Comer announced he wants to interview Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche as part of the probe and said he is in communication with the DOJ about scheduling. Epstein's longtime executive secretary Lesley Groff also testified before the panel, describing Epstein as a 'master manipulator' and saying she was unaware of his crimes.

During his closed-door testimony before the House Oversight Committee, Bill Gates revealed that Epstein attempted to use Gates's extramarital affairs as leverage to pressure him into maintaining their relationship. Rep. Robert Garcia (D-Calif.) publicly condemned Gates's ties to Epstein as 'really troubling,' noting the association began after Epstein's 2008 guilty plea to sex crimes.

Four House Republicans who pushed for the release of Epstein files, identifying themselves as 'The Bravehearts,' are facing political consequences for acting against Trump's fierce opposition to the move, according to NBC News.

Real estate heiress Tanya Dick-Stock and her husband filed a $15 billion lawsuit against Barclays and HSBC, alleging the banks enabled her late father to launder money through trusts, including one valued at $350 million, with a reported link to Ghislaine Maxwell. Rep. Robert Garcia sent a letter to House Oversight Committee Chair James Comer urging him to call JD Vance and White House officials to testify following reports of Trump administration efforts to contain the Epstein scandal.

The New York Times published an investigative piece in which four of its journalists discussed unanswered questions surrounding Epstein's death during his final weeks in jail, alongside a separate summary of key findings about Epstein's case and his associates. Questions have also emerged about whether a White House official recorded and leaked sensitive Epstein-related discussions held in the Situation Room, according to the Washington Examiner.

Congressional staffers from the House Judiciary and House Oversight Committees toured the minimum-security prison camp in Texas where Ghislaine Maxwell is incarcerated, with Reps. Jamie Raskin and Robert Garcia releasing a joint statement describing the facility as a 'park-like campus.'

Alan Dershowitz is scheduled to appear before the House Oversight Committee on July 20 for a closed-door, transcribed interview about his ties to Jeffrey Epstein, according to sources familiar with the planning.

Bill Gates testified before a House panel that Jeffrey Epstein attempted to blackmail him by threatening to expose information about Gates' extramarital affairs to compel his continued association with Epstein. The New York Times published a separate investigative piece examining Epstein's childhood and early life, exploring behavioral patterns from his boyhood years.

A transcript of Bill Gates' closed-door House Oversight Committee testimony was released publicly, confirming his account that Epstein 'contemplated blackmailing' him using information about his extramarital affairs. Ghislaine Maxwell filed new legal challenges to her 2021 sex-trafficking conviction, arguing that recently released Epstein files expose violations that invalidate her conviction.
A federal judge in Washington, D.C. issued a preliminary injunction ordering the Department of Justice to unredact additional pages of Epstein files or explain why it cannot do so.

The federal judge's July 2 deadline was newly confirmed as the compliance window for the DOJ's unredaction order. Leon Black testified before the House Oversight Committee, telling Congress that Jeffrey Epstein 'duped and deceived' him, according to Reuters. House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer issued two subpoenas to Black, who had previously refused to answer questions before the committee.

The US and Iran are holding nuclear talks in Geneva aimed at resolving their nuclear dispute, with President Trump accompanying diplomatic efforts with military threats and a Middle East force buildup.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated progress has been made in negotiations with Iran after the U.S. sent a draft peace proposal to Tehran.
Following US-Israeli attacks on key infrastructure, Iranian hardliners and politicians are demanding withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.
Iranian President Pezeshkian released a letter to Americans on X hours before Trump's scheduled address on Iran operations.
Iran rejected a U.S. ceasefire deal and instead conveyed a 10-point counterproposal through Pakistani intermediaries. The proposal demanded an end to ongoing attacks and an end to sanctions.

Pakistan has been mediating backchannel talks between the United States and Iran, with U.S. Vice President JD Vance involved in the mediation efforts. Iran has sought indirect engagement through the U.S. vice president.
Iran's ambassador to Pakistan stated that an Iranian delegation is scheduled to arrive in Islamabad on Thursday.
Negotiations between the U.S. and Iran are being hosted in Islamabad as both sides seek a diplomatic off-ramp to the conflict.

High-stakes U.S.-Iran negotiations were set for Islamabad this weekend, with Vice President JD Vance leading the American delegation in talks aimed at ending the war and finalizing ceasefire terms. The White House described the talks as ongoing, while Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei stated through state TV that Iran does not want war and seeks compensation. Some Republicans in Congress moved to assert legislative authority over any lasting deal with Tehran, citing a 2015 Obama-era law. China's role in the negotiations was also under discussion, with NBC News correspondent Janis Mackey Frayer covering that dimension of the diplomacy.

Vice President JD Vance traveled to Islamabad, Pakistan, to lead U.S. talks with Iranian officials aimed at ending the ongoing conflict, stating he expects 'positive' negotiations and that President Trump provided 'pretty clear guidelines' for the discussions. Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf posted on X that Iran will not negotiate with the U.S. without a ceasefire in Lebanon and the release of blocked Iranian assets, adding that two mutually agreed-upon measures have yet to be implemented. A fragile ceasefire remains in place, though multiple hurdles continue to strain it.

US and Iranian delegations convened in Islamabad, Pakistan, for high-stakes nuclear and diplomatic talks, with Pakistan serving as host and mediator. Vice President JD Vance participated on the US side, and a US plane carrying the American team was confirmed to have landed in Islamabad by two Pakistani sources. A fragile ceasefire between the US and Iran is currently in place, with the Strait of Hormuz among the key issues under negotiation.

Vice President JD Vance traveled to Islamabad, Pakistan on Saturday for direct talks with Iranian officials, the first such direct U.S.-Iran negotiations since 1979. The White House confirmed the talks, with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif playing a mediating role in hosting the negotiations. A two-week ceasefire between the U.S. and Iran, described as fragile, remains in effect, and Iran is seeking sanctions relief as part of the discussions. Special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner participated in trilateral talks with Iranian officials, drawing criticism from Sen. Mark Kelly. The Strait of Hormuz remains a key factor in the negotiations. Separately, Saudi Arabia confirmed that Pakistan sent fighter jets to the kingdom under a mutual defense pact.
After approximately 21 hours of negotiations in Pakistan, Vice President JD Vance announced that no deal was reached between the U.S. and Iran, describing the outcome as 'bad news for Iran.'

Trump initially told CNBC he did not want to extend the ceasefire with Iran, but ultimately announced an extension before the deadline expired. The extension is conditional, remaining in effect until Iran submits a proposal and discussions are concluded, while the blockade against Iran stays in place.

Iran submitted a response to a U.S. peace proposal aimed at ending the war, according to Iranian state media outlet IRNA. No details of Iran's response or the contents of the U.S. proposal have been publicly disclosed.

Trump claimed in a Fox News interview with Sean Hannity that during his talks with Xi Jinping in Beijing, Xi offered to help with Iran, specifically related to keeping the Strait of Hormuz open. Trump also stated that Xi committed to not providing military equipment to Iran, describing the pledge as significant.

Trump stated that the United States will retrieve uranium from Iran, reflecting tensions over its enrichment activities. Iranian Supreme Leader Khamenei has ordered that enriched uranium remain inside Iran rather than be transferred elsewhere. The U.S. Senate advanced a bill aimed at ending the war with Iran, with Senator Cassidy switching his position to support the measure after losing a primary election.

Trump announced via Truth Social on Saturday that a deal with Iran is 'largely negotiated,' stating that 'Final aspects and details of the Deal are currently being discussed, and will be announced shortly,' following a phone call with Gulf and regional Arab leaders to review Iran's latest proposal. The proposed deal would include reopening the Strait of Hormuz and formally ending the war between the U.S. and Iran. Secretary of State Marco Rubio separately stated that 'significant progress' has been made in negotiations. However, Iran and Iranian state media dismissed Trump's characterization as inconsistent with reality, and a senior Iranian source told Reuters that Iran has not agreed to hand over its highly enriched uranium stockpile, contradicting U.S. officials cited by the NY Times who said Iran had agreed to relinquish enriched uranium. Republican war hawks urged Trump to abandon peace efforts, and Senator Lindsey Graham raised concerns about the potential agreement, while details of what has formally been agreed upon remain unclear.
The White House dismissed an outline of an 'unofficial' Iran deal, according to the NY Times.

Wall Street investors are broadly assuming a U.S.-Iran nuclear deal would be a net positive for stocks and risky assets, though analysts also raise the possibility it could trigger a market selloff. Separately, analysts suggest oil prices may not return to previous lower levels even after the conflict concludes.

Trump announced he is convening advisers in the White House Situation Room to make a 'final determination' on a deal with Iran, posting the announcement via social media. Trump also demanded that Arab and Muslim countries normalize relations with Israel through the Abraham Accords as a condition for ending the conflict, a last-minute linkage that U.S. allies pushed back against, according to NBC News. Former national security adviser John Bolton publicly called the tentative deal 'a big defeat for the United States' and a 'mistake,' alleging it is driven by Trump's concerns over high gas prices ahead of midterm elections.

Iranian state media announced the suspension of all peace talks with the United States following U.S. and Israeli strikes. Trump described the negotiations as 'very boring' and told CNBC he 'couldn't care less' if they break down. IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi stated that the 2015 JCPOA is no longer a workable model and that any future nuclear agreement with Iran will look significantly different.
The IAEA released its first report on Iran's nuclear programme since February, finding little change in the programme despite the ongoing conflict in the region, according to Reuters.
The IAEA reiterated concerns that Iran's suspension of cooperation with the agency has prevented inspectors from fully monitoring Iran's nuclear program since 2025.
The US is preparing a draft resolution to condemn Iran at the IAEA, according to diplomats cited by Newsmax.
Trump claimed Iran made a 'big' promise not to develop nuclear weapons, but nuclear experts noted Iran has formally maintained this pledge for over 50 years, according to the NY Times.

IAEA chief described Iran-U.S. nuclear talks as being in a 'complicated phase.' Trump stated in a Financial Times interview that Israel 'won't have any choice' but to accept any potential deal with Iran, repeating that he 'calls all the shots' regarding U.S.-Israel decisions.
The IAEA Board of Governors passed a resolution demanding that Iran report its uranium stockpiles, according to Reuters.

The U.S. and Iran announced they are closing in on a final agreement potentially signable as soon as Sunday or Monday, which could launch further talks to wind down Iran's nuclear program, reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and end military hostilities. Pakistan's Prime Minister stated the two sides have agreed on the wording of a deal, per AP News. Trump expressed anger after Iranian state media leaked purported deal details, even as he publicly praised the agreement. The UAE reportedly agreed to release $10–$20 billion in frozen Iranian assets as a goodwill gesture, with $3 billion said to already be transferred, though the UAE foreign ministry denied the transfer. A senior U.S. official confirmed a potential deal would include economic rewards for Iran if it meets its obligations. Iran's new leadership is assessed by U.S. analysts as more willing to withstand pressure, believing it has already absorbed the worst military and economic pressure America and Israel can inflict.

Senior Trump administration officials briefed reporters on a 14-point memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Iran, with Vice President Vance signing the MOU on behalf of the United States in Switzerland on Friday. The deal includes sanctions relief on Iranian oil and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Trump simultaneously described the MOU as 'not final' and threatened to resume airstrikes if Iran does not comply, while at the G7 summit in France he called it 'a very strong deal' even while acknowledging 'nobody knows what it is.' Trump dismissed reports of a $300 billion rebuilding fund for Iran as false, and the White House disputed leaked draft versions of the agreement. G7 leaders issued a joint declaration supporting the agreement, with Canadian PM Carney calling it 'a game changer,' though Republican lawmakers expressed significant skepticism and the full text had not yet been publicly released. Trump thanked Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin for remaining neutral during the U.S.-Iran conflict, and the NY Times published what a senior U.S. official described as the full text of the deal.

The EU announced it will not lift key sanctions on Iran until a formal nuclear deal is officially reached, maintaining economic pressure during the 60-day negotiating period that began following Trump's signing of the 14-point MOU.

Nuclear talks resumed as U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff traveled to Switzerland, with Switzerland confirming negotiations are continuing at the Bürgenstock resort while declining to identify participants. Iran's delegation departed for Switzerland after a delay caused by fighting in Lebanon, though Iranian officials publicly downplayed progress toward a deal. Iran warned it would take 'reciprocal action' if the U.S. fails to honor MOU commitments, while Iran's rival political factions entered open conflict over the agreement domestically. Trump defended the MOU on Saturday, attacking critics as 'Radical Left fools and Dumocrats' and slamming Obama after the former president and several lawmakers spoke out against the deal's terms. Nuclear experts warned the framework could leave Tehran with excessive control over its uranium stockpile due to insufficient IAEA inspection requirements. Reuters reported that Iran's Revolutionary Guards stand to gain significantly from their extensive business empire if U.S. sanctions are lifted.

Following two days of talks in Switzerland, Vice President Vance announced on Monday that Iran agreed to allow IAEA nuclear inspectors back into the country and that both sides agreed on a roadmap toward a final deal within 60 days, describing the talks as laying a 'good foundation.' The U.S. Treasury Department issued a 60-day general license temporarily allowing the sale of Iranian oil, with U.S. oil prices falling below $74 a barrel as markets anticipated increased Iranian crude supply. Qatar and Pakistan are serving as mediators in the negotiations.

Iran released a contradictory statement through its foreign ministry claiming it made 'no new commitments' on nuclear inspections, directly undercutting Vance's announcement that Iran had agreed to allow IAEA inspectors back into the country. The U.S. announced it will release $12 billion in frozen Iranian funds alongside the oil sanctions waiver, with Al Jazeera citing Iran's commitment to inspections as the stated justification. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian traveled to Pakistan following the Switzerland talks. A CBS News poll found most Americans want the war with Iran to end but relatively few believe the U.S. secured the better terms in the agreement. Senate Republicans are scheduled for a tense Wednesday meeting with Trump on Capitol Hill to discuss the emerging Iran deal alongside the SAVE America Act, as Republican lawmakers who opposed the Obama-era deal voice parallel concerns about Trump's framework.

The Senate approved a House-passed war powers resolution directing Trump to halt U.S. armed forces from hostilities against Iran, marking the first time such a measure has passed both chambers since the conflict began; the resolution is characterized as largely symbolic and non-binding, with some Republicans joining Democrats in support. Iran's foreign ministry issued a further denial of IAEA inspection commitments, contradicting both Vance's earlier announcement and Trump's public statement that Iran had agreed to nuclear inspections. Secretary of State Rubio began a three-day Gulf tour covering the UAE, Kuwait, and Bahrain to brief allies on the preliminary U.S.-Iran agreement. Trump posted on Truth Social announcing he had agreed to allow the Strait of Hormuz to remain open with no further naval blockade, though Newsweek reported confusion surrounding the statement; Iran separately insisted on maintaining control of the strait following the Switzerland talks. Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz increased following the U.S.-Iran deal, with 42 ships passing through on Saturday alone, and the UN announced an evacuation plan to move stranded ships through the waterway.

The IAEA head signaled that nuclear inspectors would visit Iranian enrichment sites, describing it as a key component of the interim deal, even as Iran's government continued to deny making new commitments on inspections. Secretary of State Rubio arrived in Abu Dhabi to brief Gulf allies on the U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding, describing efforts to secure allied support as 'a work in progress.' The White House accused mainstream media of 'parroting' Iranian regime propaganda amid ongoing public disputes over the deal's terms. An Economist/YouGov poll found 48 percent of Republicans oppose the $300 billion reconstruction fund for Iran included in Trump's plan, with only 23 percent in support. Trump allies separately moved to reassure Israeli officials over rising tensions linked to the nuclear negotiations, according to Al Jazeera.

Trump and Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.) had a loud, intense confrontation during a closed-door Capitol meeting on Wednesday. The U.S. Department of Homeland Security announced it is easing travel restrictions for Iran's World Cup team, allowing the squad to enter the country two days before their next match.

A media outlet linked to Iran's IRGC declared that Iran has 'no choice' but to develop a nuclear bomb to protect 'peace and calm,' directly contradicting Iran's pledge to the Trump administration as part of the ongoing nuclear negotiations.
Russia launched drone and missile strikes on Ukrainian cities and infrastructure near the time of scheduled US-Ukraine talks in Geneva.
A Russian-operated gas tanker sank in the Mediterranean Sea following a Ukrainian drone attack, which Russia attributed to Ukraine.
A Russian-flagged gas tanker sank in the Mediterranean Sea following a drone attack that Russia attributed to Ukraine.
Russian publication Izvestia reported that Ukraine peace talks have been paused in connection with the Iran war.
Ukraine reported hitting a Russian oil terminal at Primorsk and a refinery in Ufa on Monday.
Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine has evidence that Russia is supplying Iran with intelligence.
Russia launched a large drone attack on Ukrainian cities including Lviv, damaging a UNESCO World Heritage site and injuring multiple people.
Ukrainian President Zelenskiy stated that the US has linked security guarantees to Ukraine ceding Donbas territory.
Ukrainian President Zelenskiy stated that the US has linked security guarantees to Ukraine giving up Donbas, according to Reuters.
Zelensky visited Saudi Arabia and offered Ukraine's drone expertise.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky made a surprise visit to Saudi Arabia to offer Ukraine's drone defense expertise developed during the war against Russia to the U.S. and Gulf States.
Russia announced a ban on gasoline exports starting April 1.
Russian strikes on Ukraine killed 4 people, and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed openness to diverting weapons to Kyiv.
Ukrainian drones damaged Russia's Ust-Luga port, causing a fire to break out.
President Zelenskyy stated in an NBC News interview that he hopes President Trump cares about Ukraine's future, noting that Trump administration priorities center on the United States.
Ukraine's president stated that allies asked him about reducing attacks on Russian energy as prices rise due to the Iran war.
Estonia's defence forces detected an air threat overnight.
Ukraine's president hosted EU leaders at an event marking the Bucha massacre anniversary while Ukraine's negotiator Umerov was in Turkey for talks.
A Russian military transport plane crashed in Crimea, killing 29 people, according to the Russian Defense Ministry.
A Russian military transport plane crashed in Crimea, killing 29 people. Officials cited possible technical malfunction.
Russia is recruiting students for its drone forces in Ukraine and offering large financial packages as part of recruitment efforts.
Ukrainian President Zelensky warned about Russia's intelligence sharing with Iran in an exclusive NewsNation interview and discussed Ukraine's assistance to the US in its conflict with Iran.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned in an exclusive interview about Russia's intelligence sharing with Iran and discussed how Ukraine is helping the US in its war against Iran.
Fuel leaks occurred at Russia's Primorsk oil facility and a fire broke out at the NORSI oil refinery in Nizhny Novgorod, according to Russian authorities.
Zelenskiy traveled to Syria and met with President Sharaa.
A child was rescued from rubble after a Russian strike collapsed a home in Odesa, killing at least three people.
The Iran war has driven shortages and price spikes across multiple consumer product categories beyond oil and gas, including beer cans, helium balloons, and mortgages.

Farmers warned that the Iran war and its associated costs would drive up their expenses and subsequently affect food prices, with the recently announced ceasefire not expected to immediately relieve those pressures.

Vladimir Putin announced a ceasefire coinciding with Orthodox Easter weekend, including April 12, and both Russia and Ukraine signaled agreement to the truce. President Zelensky stated that Ukraine will complete repairs to the Druzhba oil pipeline in spring and said peace talks to end the war could resume soon, though he expressed skepticism about any imminent breakthrough.

A 32-hour Easter truce was established between Ukraine and Russia, though both Ukrainians and Russians expressed doubt it would lead to lasting peace. Russian casualties are mounting, recruitment is falling, and territorial gains are dwindling, while Ukraine has been increasing drone production. President Zelensky traveled to the Middle East in March, securing a series of 10-year agreements with Gulf State leaders, and subsequently announced that Ukrainian interceptors had downed Iranian drones in the region, with 228 Ukrainian experts previously deployed there.

Russian drone strikes killed at least two people in the Ukrainian city of Odesa overnight into Saturday, according to local authorities. A Ukrainian drone attack in Russia's Kursk region injured three people, as reported by the regional governor. Separately, Ukraine and Russia exchanged 175 servicemen each ahead of an Easter ceasefire.
Russia launched one of the most intense aerial attacks of the year on Ukraine, sending hundreds of drones and missiles overnight in a hours-long assault targeting civilian areas across the country.
Vladimir Putin declared his belief that the war with Ukraine is 'coming to an end' as a new three-day ceasefire went into effect.
Ukraine launched one of its largest drone attacks on Russia, killing at least four people, three of them in the Moscow region.

Russia conducted joint military exercises with Belarus that included delivering nuclear warheads to Belarusian sites, with the drills described as rehearsals for the use of nuclear forces. Ukraine conducted attacks targeting Russian energy infrastructure sites as part of ongoing military operations.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard threatened a 'completely different' escalatory response following the latest U.S. self-defense strikes. International oil prices jumped 6 percent on Monday, reaching levels not seen since mid-May, after Iran reportedly cut off nuclear talks with the United States; analysts warned prices could climb further if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed. President Trump sent proposed edits to a potential Iran agreement addressing points about the Strait of Hormuz and enriched uranium, while posting on Truth Social urging Democrats and what he called 'seemingly unpatriotic Republicans' to stop 'chirping' about the negotiations, stating Iran 'really wants to make a deal.'
Rep. Ashley Hinson, a Trump ally, warned that a potential war with Iran risks becoming a political liability for the Republican Party, according to Newsmax.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio testified before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee and the House Appropriations Committee on Tuesday regarding the State Department's FY2027 budget request, marking his first congressional testimony since the start of the war. During the Senate hearing, Rubio clashed with Sen. Cory Booker, who accused the Trump administration of strengthening Iran's geopolitical position; Rubio pushed back and stated that the destruction of Iran's military has eliminated the country's ability to use a 'conventional shield' to protect its nuclear program, dismissing the Iranian Navy as 'a bunch of Boston Whalers with machine guns.' DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin also testified before a Senate appropriations subcommittee Tuesday on the DHS FY2027 budget request. Reuters reported Iran is studying a deal to halt the war as a stalemate persists, while former National Security Adviser John Bolton claimed Iran believes it can outlast Trump in negotiations, citing oil price pressures as leverage. The U.S. is also reportedly pressing Oman to cut its ties with Iran, according to Newsmax.

An Iranian drone attack struck Kuwait's main airport, causing injuries and prompting Kuwait to suspend commercial flights, occurring hours after Iran and the U.S. traded missile strikes in the region. U.S. Central Command announced that U.S. forces fired a Hellfire missile at a Botswana-flagged oil tanker sailing toward an Iranian port in the Arabian Gulf. Iran's IRGC launched attacks on the U.S. Fifth Fleet headquarters and an airbase, according to Iranian local media cited by Reuters. CBS News sources reported that the U.S. fighter pilot whose jet was downed over Iran in April had previously been shot down by Kuwaiti friendly fire at the start of the war. Oil prices jumped following the latest missile exchanges in the region.

The U.S. House is set to vote on a measure directing President Trump to halt military engagement in Iran, after Republican leaders can no longer delay the vote. The European Commission warned the EU could lose 1.3 million jobs due to energy price surges linked to the conflict. Rep. Ashley Hinson stated in audio obtained by CBS News that the conflict could become a political liability if it extends beyond the next few weeks. National Review characterized the subsequent ceasefire as a disappointment for the Trump administration despite describing the conflict itself as a tactical triumph.

The House passed a war powers resolution 215-208 on Wednesday to restrict President Trump's authority to engage U.S. forces in hostilities with Iran without congressional approval, marking the first time the House has passed such a resolution since the conflict began. Four Republicans, including Thomas Massie (Ky.) and Brian Fitzpatrick (Pa.), voted with Democrats to pass the measure, though it would likely face a presidential veto even if the Senate approves it. Iran launched deadly strikes on U.S. bases in Kuwait on Wednesday, describing the attacks as self-defense, while Kuwait's defence ministry condemned the airport attack as 'heinous Iranian aggression' and released CCTV footage it says shows the Iranian drone strike. Trump told reporters Wednesday he is 'very proud' of the decision to strike Iran and claimed the war has coincided with record stock market gains, though Reuters reported stocks declined following the latest flare-up of hostilities and the OECD warned a prolonged energy supply disruption could trigger recessions and increased unemployment globally. Trump indicated nuclear talks with Iran remain ongoing despite the strikes. Marc Short, former chief of staff to Vice President Pence, published a Washington Post op-ed warning the war and Trump's trade policy could cost Republicans the support of farmers.

Trump condemned the four Republican lawmakers who voted with Democrats to pass the war powers resolution as 'unpatriotic' and 'bad,' and dismissed the resolution itself as 'meaningless.' The White House confirmed it continues to pursue diplomatic negotiations with Iran over its nuclear program nearly two months after the fragile ceasefire, despite repeated Iranian military provocations.
An Economist/YouGov poll found that 68% of Americans said the U.S. should make a deal to end the war in Iran 'as quickly as possible,' while 11% disagreed and 21% were undecided.

The UN World Food Programme warned that the US-Iran war is causing substantial increases in food prices across multiple countries, pushing millions into food crisis. A US naval blockade has cost Iran nearly $6 billion in oil revenues, with Iran now exporting less than one-sixth of pre-war oil volumes, according to Al Jazeera. Iran announced it fired warning missiles and drones at US warships in the Gulf of Oman, and U.S. forces boarded a sanctioned tanker in the Indian Ocean, according to the Pentagon.

US Central Command confirmed that at least four Iranian drones launched toward the Strait of Hormuz were shot down, with CENTCOM stating the drones posed an immediate threat to regional maritime traffic. US forces subsequently struck Iranian coastal radar sites at Goruk in Hormozgan province and on Qeshm Island in response to the drone launch. President Trump stated that Iran retains approximately 21-22% of its missiles and claimed most of Iran's drone factories, launching pads, and missile manufacturing facilities have been destroyed, as peace talks continue.
President Trump stated that Iran 'has no choice' but to reach a deal to end the war, according to Newsmax.

The US and Iranian forces engaged in their most intense exchange since a ceasefire began, straining the fragile truce, with the US shooting down Iranian drones over the Strait of Hormuz on what marked day 100 of the conflict. The Treasury Department is considering using frozen Iranian assets to fund reconstruction efforts for Gulf allies damaged by Iranian attacks. A former US ambassador told Newsweek that American vulnerabilities exposed over the 100-day conflict stem from political rather than military failures, while analysts identified China, Iran, and Israel as relative winners of the period. Economists are revisiting the concept of 'demand destruction' as oil price spikes persist.

At the 100-day mark, U.S. households have spent an average of $750 more in expenses, with middle- and lower-income Americans bearing the greatest burden, according to Al Jazeera. Global airlines slashed their 2026 profit forecasts due to the fuel price shock caused by the conflict. The United States circulated a draft IAEA resolution demanding Iran provide greater transparency about its nuclear sites and uranium stockpiles. Trump, in his NBC Meet the Press interview, defended a compensation fund and reiterated that gas prices would fall when the war ends. The NY Times reported widespread despair among Iranians across the political spectrum amid a collapsing economy and skyrocketing inflation.
Trump faces mounting challenges in managing the Iran crisis, according to the NY Times, echoing difficulties experienced by previous administrations despite his campaign promises.

Iran shot down a U.S. Army AH-64 Apache helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz late Monday night, with both crew members rescued uninjured by the U.S. Navy unmanned surface vessel Saronic Corsair. Trump announced the incident and a forthcoming U.S. response via social media on Tuesday. Separately, the crew of a sanctioned oil tanker sent a distress call and were rescued off the coast of Oman after the vessel was struck by a missile fired from a U.S. fighter jet. U.S. forces also fired on a tanker that was reportedly attempting to evade a blockade.

The U.S. military launched retaliatory strikes against Iran on Tuesday, which CENTCOM described as a 'proportional response' and 'self-defense' following the helicopter downing. Iran responded by targeting U.S. bases in Jordan and the Gulf. Analyst Trita Parsi told Al Jazeera that Iran has abandoned strategic patience in favor of a new doctrine of swift, severe retaliation in response to any U.S. attack.

On Wednesday, Trump told reporters the U.S. would continue striking Iran 'very hard' and that Iran 'will have to pay the price' for slow negotiations, also warning of attacks on civilian infrastructure including power plants and bridges. Trump posted on Truth Social that Iran's military is 'a complete and total mess' and separately claimed it is 'completely defeated,' while also asserting that the U.S. naval blockade is crushing Iran's economy. U.S. strikes hit several sites in Iran including water facilities, with Al Jazeera reporting Iran's counter-strikes targeted U.S. military assets in Kuwait and Bahrain. Al Jazeera analysts reported Iran's strategic goal is to deter American patrols in the Strait of Hormuz as the exchange of strikes continued to escalate. The U.S. also imposed new sanctions on China- and Hong Kong-based entities for weapons dealings with Iran, and a Reuters survey found OPEC oil output fell to its lowest level since at least 2000 amid continued pressure on Iranian production.

Iran announced the closure of the Strait of Hormuz to all vessels following a second consecutive day of U.S. military strikes on Wednesday evening, causing oil prices to rise. U.S. strikes hit targets on Qeshm Island and ports along the Strait of Hormuz, and a Palau-flagged oil tanker was struck off the coast of Oman, killing three Indian sailors. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth pledged further strikes on 'key facilities' and warned of 'strong and clear' action on Wednesday and Thursday nights if needed, with CENTCOM citing Iran's 'unwarranted and continued aggression' as justification. Reuters sources reported Iran is seeking funds as nuclear talks move toward a potential interim deal, while the escalating exchanges threatened to collapse ceasefire efforts and created political complications for Trump ahead of midterm elections. Nikki Haley called on Trump to threaten Russia and China with force over their military aid to Iran.

Trump posted a threat on Truth Social on June 11 to seize Iran's Kharg Island, its major oil export hub, and stated the U.S. would take 'total control' of Iran's oil and gas markets, while also expressing doubt that American voters have the 'stomach' for the operation. Trump subsequently canceled planned Thursday strikes citing progress toward a peace deal, indicating an announcement could come 'shortly,' though he also stated the U.S. would hit Iran 'very hard' that night. CENTCOM launched strikes on Thursday targeting Iranian military surveillance, communication systems, and air defense sites, marking a second consecutive day of U.S. strikes, while Iran's IRGC claimed it struck 18 targets at U.S. bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan. The U.S. denied Iran had successfully closed the Strait of Hormuz, and Al Jazeera reported that Trump's claim of smuggling 100 million barrels of oil through the strait did not add up mathematically. India lodged a formal protest after three Indian mariners were killed in U.S. strikes on tankers off Oman, with a third tanker crewed by Indians struck in a suspected separate incident; Oman's military rescued dozens of Indian seafarers from struck vessels. The Pentagon released video of missile launches describing strikes as self-defense, while Trump and Hegseth publicly pre-announced strike plans, departing from standard military practice, and Hegseth dismissed questions about civilian infrastructure strikes as war crimes as 'disingenuous.'

Trump announced the cancellation of planned military strikes on Iran, citing proximity to a negotiated deal, with oil prices falling in response. Rep. Kevin Kiley called for congressional involvement in any final agreement following the cancellation. Iranians expressed mixed emotions of fear and relief over the ongoing uncertainty, per the NY Times, while UK economic data from April showed the Iran war beginning to affect its economy. The NY Times noted that two months after a nominal ceasefire, Iran, Israel, and the U.S. remain engaged in low-intensity conflict with no clear resolution.

Newsweek documented a pattern of Trump repeatedly threatening military strikes against Iran only to cancel them with hours or minutes to spare. Tucker Carlson criticized Trump on his show for 'overselling' the military operation and asserted that Iran now controls the Strait of Hormuz. Sen. Adam Schiff accused Trump of 'telling falsehood after falsehood' about the state of negotiations. Republican strategists and county chairs are privately pressuring the Trump administration to exit the Iran conflict by Labor Day, warning continued involvement could damage the party in midterm elections, according to Politico.
U.S. forces shot down Iranian attack drones in an undisclosed engagement, according to a Reuters source.

Trump warned that 'all hell will rain down' on Iran if it attempts to acquire a nuclear weapon. The NY Times reported that US officials have neither publicly acknowledged responsibility for a February 28 strike that hit an Iranian school nor released findings from an investigation into the resulting deaths.

The US Senate narrowly voted to block a new measure that would have reined in Trump's war powers, according to Reuters. Sen. Raphael Warnock called on Congress to assert itself on matters related to the Iran war in a CBS News interview.

President Trump signed a 14-point memorandum of understanding with Iran at Versailles during a visit with French President Macron, with Iranian President Pezeshkian also signing remotely; the White House announced the MOU came into effect immediately, with a planned in-person signing in Switzerland on Friday. The deal includes a ceasefire in Lebanon, reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a $300 billion reconstruction plan for Iran, and future sanctions relief, with U.S. officials describing it as 'performance-based,' meaning Iran receives benefits as it demonstrates compliance. Trump defended the deal at the G7, threatened to resume bombing if Iran violates its terms, and stated it was 'unfair' for Iran not to retain ballistic missiles if neighboring countries possess them. The agreement drew criticism from conservative allies who called it one of the most humiliating in U.S. diplomatic history, while former Biden Iran envoy Robert Malley called it 'far preferable to any of the alternatives,' and Pope Leo XIV welcomed the deal. Asian stock markets hit record highs and oil prices fell following the signing, with average U.S. gasoline prices dropping below $4 for the first time in months after Pakistan confirmed the Strait of Hormuz reopening would take effect immediately. BBC News reported the deal's text falls short of Trump's claim that it prevents Iran from ever acquiring nuclear weapons, with core sticking points including Iran's nuclear program deferred to later negotiations.

Obama publicly criticized the Trump administration's handling of the Iran war, stating the U.S. may be 'worse off' than before and has spent billions of dollars while putting enormous strain on its military. An AP-NORC poll found a majority of Americans disapprove of Trump's Iran handling, with 37% approving and 62% disapproving of his presidency overall. Planned nuclear talks in Switzerland were canceled after Vice President Vance scrapped his planned trip, with the White House acknowledging logistical unpredictability; delays were also linked to renewed Israel-Hezbollah hostilities. Republican critics directed blame for the Iran MOU at Vance rather than Trump directly, while Senate Democratic Leader Schumer called the deal 'the art of the surrender' and Sen. Ted Cruz criticized plans to give 'billions' to Iran. Iran's Supreme Leader Khamenei publicly distanced himself from the framework, stating he dislikes it but allowed it to proceed, placing responsibility on Iran's president. Wikipedia listed the conflict's outcome as an 'Iranian Victory,' a characterization experts told Newsweek makes a U.S. triumph difficult to claim, and the Pentagon was reported by Newsmax to be seeking $80 billion to cover war-related costs.

Trump told Axios in a post-G7 interview that he sees 'no limits' to his power amid the war with Iran and claimed Israel does what he says. Iran's deputy foreign minister stated Iran is 'ready to move forward' on diplomacy but conditioned engagement on the US ensuring Israel ends its attacks on Lebanon. National Review published commentary framing Trump's Iran policy as a 'capitulation,' while Senator Tuberville expressed support for the deal's nuclear progress and at least one Democratic lawmaker criticized it as 'surrender.'

U.S. and Iranian delegations convened at Burgenstock, Switzerland, for talks mediated by Qatar and Pakistan, with Lebanon atop the agenda on day 114 of the Iran war. Analysts cited by the NY Times assessed that neither the war nor Trump's deal succeeded in eliminating the main threats posed by Iran. Democrats framed the conflict as economically painful with no positive results, while Republicans remained divided, with some expressing relief at falling gas prices.

The Senate passed a war powers resolution directing Trump to end U.S. military involvement in the Iran conflict, marking the first time the Senate has approved such a measure; four Republican senators voted in favor of the largely symbolic, non-binding resolution. A Reuters/Ipsos poll of 1,262 U.S. adults found only 24 percent of Americans believe the war with Iran was worth its costs. The U.S. and Iran issued conflicting public statements over nuclear inspections and the status of the Strait of Hormuz as negotiators continued pushing toward a final comprehensive deal. Trump promoted falling oil and gas prices tied to the preliminary peace agreement during a campaign swing in Pennsylvania.

Survivors and families of the Iranian drone strike in Kuwait on March 1 accused the Pentagon of downplaying injuries from the attack, with one wounded soldier telling CBS News he 'absolutely' believes the Army and Pentagon have minimized the incident.

The Senate voted late Wednesday night to reject the war powers resolution it had passed the prior day, after key Republican senators switched their votes following a heated closed-door meeting with President Trump at the Capitol. Trump engaged in a lengthy and angry exchange with Sen. Bill Cassidy of Louisiana and other Republicans who had voted to limit his war powers, with Cassidy acknowledging he lost his temper and Trump raising his voice; Trump afterward publicly characterized the party as 'really well unified.' The White House formally requested $87.6 billion in supplemental funding from Congress in a letter from OMB Director Russ Vought to House Speaker Mike Johnson, with approximately $67 billion designated for the Pentagon to cover Iran war costs, alongside farm aid and Ebola response funding, though the package faces significant congressional opposition. Trump stated he does not believe the U.S. is liable for a missile strike on an Iranian girls' school that reportedly killed hundreds of children, adding that it may never be known who was responsible. Trump also criticized NATO for insufficient participation in the Iran war during a conversation with Secretary General Mark Rutte, who cited Alliance use of U.S. bases in Europe as evidence of support; Rutte visited the White House ahead of the upcoming NATO summit with Iran among the key topics. Iran's football team trip to Seattle was delayed after player Mehdi Taremi and an assistant coach were held up by U.S. officials at the airport, and fertilizer prices declined following the Strait of Hormuz reopening, though farmers are not expected to see meaningful relief for several months.

Trump visited Capitol Hill and chastised Republican senators who had voted to limit his war powers, after which the Senate reversed its earlier war powers resolution vote from 50-48 against to 50-47 in favor. Trump stated the reversal 'puts Iran on notice' as U.S.-Iran negotiations over a long-term deal continue. Trump also canceled the signing of a bipartisan housing bill during the same visit, reiterating demands for Congress to pass the SAVE America Act.

The Senate's reversal of the war powers resolution was confirmed as final after Sens. Bill Cassidy and another key Republican switched their votes following Trump's Capitol Hill visit. Iran's men's national football team is set to play Friday at the 2026 FIFA World Cup after securing two draws against New Zealand. The PCE index rose 4.1% year-over-year in May, its highest level in three years, according to CBS News.

U.S. Central Command conducted retaliatory strikes on Friday targeting missile and drone storage locations and coastal radar positions inside Iran — the first U.S. strikes since the two countries reached a Memorandum of Understanding on June 17. The strikes came one day after Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps attacked a Singapore-flagged cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz with a drone. Iran's IRGC then struck U.S.-linked targets on Saturday, characterizing the action as a defensive response, while both sides accused the other of violating the ceasefire agreement. Bahrain also reported a drone attack amid the escalating exchanges.

CENTCOM conducted a second consecutive day of strikes on Saturday, targeting sites at Sirik and Qeshm Island, Iran, in response to continued Iranian attacks on commercial shipping near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran struck U.S.-linked military assets in Kuwait and Bahrain with drones and missiles, stating the attacks were retaliation for U.S. strikes; both Kuwait and Bahrain condemned the attacks on their territory. President Trump issued a stark warning on Truth Social that 'the Islamic Republic of Iran will no longer exist' if the U.S. is 'forced to militarily complete the job,' as the conflict expanded beyond Iranian territory to Gulf states.

Iran launched drone and missile strikes targeting U.S. allies Kuwait and Bahrain, with Kuwait's military reporting it intercepted Iranian drones and two ballistic missiles. Iran also threatened a complete halt to all negotiations with the U.S. following the continued exchange of attacks. Republican Sen. Roger Marshall stated on Meet the Press that he does not believe the conflict is over, though he described any further U.S. strikes as a 'mop-up operation.' Political scientist Robert Pape argued on Al Jazeera that the U.S. is attempting to 'squeak out of strategic defeat,' contending the fallout challenges Trump's self-image and curbs U.S. hubris.

The U.S. and Iran agreed to 'stand down' and allow commercial ships to pass through the Strait of Hormuz following a weekend of intermittent fighting, with a U.S. official confirming the arrangement to The Hill. U.S. and Iranian officials are scheduled to meet in Doha, Qatar on Tuesday to discuss the strait and broader MOU terms, according to the Washington Examiner. Oil prices rose and U.S. stock-index futures advanced on Sunday amid the renewed fighting before edging higher again once the stand-down agreement was announced, according to the Wall Street Journal, Reuters, and the NY Times. Global stocks drifted as markets absorbed news of the halt to attacks, according to Reuters.

President Trump announced that U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff will travel to Doha, Qatar on Tuesday for talks with Iran, stating that Iran requested the meeting following the weekend clashes. Iran had not confirmed its participation as of the announcement, according to Al Jazeera and CBS News. Iran's president separately announced that Qatar will release $6 billion of $12 billion in frozen Iranian assets held in the country. Mediators have established de-escalation channels ahead of the planned talks, according to a source familiar with the matter cited by Reuters.

Stock market data from Monday trading sessions in Q2 showed above-average gains, a pattern analysts have linked to weekend Iran-related news developments; the Wall Street Journal dubbed the phenomenon the 'Axios put.'

A US-Israeli military offensive against Iran began on February 27 and has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which handles approximately 20% of the world's oil supply. Iran is signaling intent to deploy mines in the critical shipping route, and shipping traffic has declined since the conflict began.
US forces destroyed 16 Iranian mine-laying vessels near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has threatened to shut down the strait, a critical shipping corridor carrying roughly 20% of the world's oil.
Three ships were attacked near the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday; Iran is linked to the attacks, which raised concerns about global oil exports and regional economic stability.
Oil and fuel prices have surged significantly, prompting the US to tap the Strategic Petroleum Reserve as part of an emergency response.

A US-Israeli military conflict with Iran has disrupted global energy markets, causing significant rises in oil and energy prices. Emergency measures are being considered to address energy price impacts.
Oil prices rose above $100 per barrel driven by military strikes on Middle East energy infrastructure amid the regional conflict.

Trump appealed to allied nations including NATO members and China to help secure or reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but allied nations have responded unenthusiastically or rebuffed the request for military support.
Trump called on other nations to help secure the Strait of Hormuz but later stated the US does not need assistance. European allies have been reluctant or unwilling to join the coalition.
U.S. Treasury Secretary stated that the United States is allowing Iranian ships to pass through the Strait of Hormuz.
A US Treasury Secretary made a public statement regarding Iranian ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz.
The Israel-Iran conflict has disrupted the Strait of Hormuz and caused oil and energy prices to rise, with broader supply chain and consumer price impacts reported.

Trump and UK Prime Minister Starmer agreed during a phone call that the Strait of Hormuz must reopen. Trump issued a 48-hour ultimatum to Iran threatening further US strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure.
President Trump announced that Iran allowed eight oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, stating Iranian negotiators informed the U.S. of this decision during ongoing negotiations.
UK ministers announced that sanctioned vessels can now be boarded by UK armed forces, prior to a sanctioned oil tanker entering UK waters.
Iran enacted a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, impacting oil prices and affecting downstream industries including fertilizer.
Two LPG tankers bound for India cleared the Strait of Hormuz, as reported by the government.
A Canadian activist captured footage of dozens of oil tankers and cargo ships in the vital Hormuz Strait waterway.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Al Jazeera that the U.S. will not accept Iran's claim over the Strait of Hormuz.
Bahrain circulated a revised UN draft regarding the Hormuz Strait that drops binding enforcement provisions.
A majority of recent ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is linked to Iran. Trump claimed Iran allowed eight oil tankers through the strait.
Two ships passed through the Strait of Hormuz and arrived at Karachi Port.
Two ships passed through the Strait of Hormuz and arrived at Karachi Port.
President Trump dismissed concerns about the Strait of Hormuz in his Wednesday night address to the nation and asserted the U.S. produces sufficient oil.
Japanese, French, and Omani vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz.

Rep. Mike Turner stated Iran's military capabilities are being significantly diminished and expressed doubt that ground troops will be necessary to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while Trump set a Tuesday deadline for Iran to open the Strait or face consequences.
Iraq urged its oil customers to send oil loading plans following a Hormuz exemption.
Libya's oil sector disputes and Hormuz tensions are creating energy supply concerns for Europe.

Trump set a Tuesday deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, threatening military strikes on Iranian infrastructure including power plants and bridges. Iran adopted a defiant stance and mobilized youth to form human chains around power plants as shields against threatened strikes. Saudi Arabia intercepted 7 missiles, with debris falling near energy facilities. A group of OPEC+ members agreed on Sunday to increase output by 206,000 barrels per day once the Strait reopens, with implementation planned for May. Asian airlines began trimming schedules and carrying extra fuel as supplies tightened amid the escalating tensions.

President Trump set an 8 p.m. EDT Tuesday deadline for Iran to agree to a peace deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, threatening 'complete demolition' of Iranian power plants and bridges and posting on Truth Social that 'a whole civilization will die tonight.' The U.S. military struck targets on Iran's Kharg Island, and the US Embassy issued a warning for Americans in Iran to evacuate or shelter in place. Russia and China vetoed a UN Security Council resolution aimed at reopening the strait, despite 11 of 15 members voting in favor and the resolution having been watered down ahead of the vote. Oil prices rose substantially and U.S. stock markets fell in response to the escalating tensions, with airlines including Delta raising checked baggage fees and ticket prices due to surging jet fuel costs. Iranian officials called on citizens to form human chains around power plants and bridges targeted in U.S. threats, while Iran's UN ambassador condemned Trump's social media post as 'deeply irresponsible.' Pakistan's Prime Minister called on Trump to extend the deadline by two weeks, VP JD Vance urged Iran to negotiate a ceasefire, and over 30 congressional Democrats called for Trump's removal via the 25th Amendment.

Trump announced a two-week ceasefire with Iran on Truth Social shortly before his stated deadline, conditional on Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran confirmed it agreed to guarantee passage through the strait for two weeks, contingent on a halt to attacks against Iran. Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif played a key diplomatic intermediary role, requesting Trump extend his deadline by two weeks to allow for further diplomacy. Oil prices fell and U.S. stock futures rose following the announcement, while Israel backed the ceasefire but stated it did not extend to Lebanon, where Israeli strikes continued. Maersk expressed caution regarding Hormuz shipping, and JPMorgan had warned gas prices could hit $5 per gallon if the strait remained closed. The UK pledged to support the ceasefire and Prime Minister Starmer announced plans to visit the Middle East, while crowds in Tehran burned U.S. and Israeli flags.

President Trump announced a two-week US-Iran ceasefire less than 90 minutes before an 8 p.m. Tuesday deadline, declaring it a 'total and complete victory' for the United States. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, alongside Joint Chiefs Chairman Dan Caine, held a Pentagon briefing declaring the military operation—named 'Operation Epic Fury'—a decisive victory, claiming Iran accepted the ceasefire 'under overwhelming pressure.' Pakistan played a key diplomatic role in brokering the deal, with Vice President JD Vance confirmed to lead the US negotiating team for follow-on talks in Islamabad; Turkish intelligence was also reported to have played a role. Stock markets rose sharply and oil prices fell following the announcement, though Iran subsequently closed the Strait of Hormuz citing Israeli strikes on Lebanon, and the ceasefire's durability remained uncertain. Iran presented a 10-point peace plan asserting its right to enrich uranium and demanding sanctions relief, while Trump insisted Iran would not be permitted to enrich uranium; Trump also announced 50% tariffs effective immediately on any country supplying military weapons to Iran. Senator Lindsey Graham described the deal as having 'troubling aspects,' Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid called it a 'political disaster,' and Vice President Vance characterized it as a 'fragile truce' contingent on Iran negotiating in good faith.

A US-Iran ceasefire was announced, sending the Dow up more than 1,000 points and causing oil prices to plunge 16% — the largest single-day drop since 2020 — as part of a deal that includes the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. However, the ceasefire was immediately strained: no oil or gas tankers transited the Strait in the first 24 hours, traders remained wary about restricted traffic, and Goldman Sachs warned crude could reach $115 by year's end. Israel launched major strikes on Lebanon shortly after the announcement, with Iran claiming this violated the ceasefire agreement and the US and Iran disputing whether Lebanon was covered; VP JD Vance characterized the disagreement as a 'legitimate misunderstanding.' Trump announced US forces deployed under Operation Epic Fury would remain in and around Iran until a permanent agreement is reached, threatened 50% tariffs on countries supplying Iran with weapons, and lashed out at European partners and NATO for not contributing militarily — NATO chief Mark Rutte met with Trump and Rubio at the White House in what he described as a 'very frank' meeting. Iran publicly released a 10-point proposal related to negotiations, which Trump dismissed on Truth Social as a 'fake ten point plan,' attacking CNN and the New York Times for their coverage. The LNG industry was described as 'scarred' by the conflict, GOP members expressed concern about Iran-related political fallout ahead of midterms, and Financial Times commentator Robert Armstrong applied his 'TACO trade' framing — 'Trump Always Chickens Out' — to Trump's abrupt policy reversal.

A two-week U.S.-Iran ceasefire took effect on Tuesday, brokered by Pakistani officials, though the Strait of Hormuz remained effectively closed with only a handful of ships transiting since the announcement, and Iran announced plans to tax oil-carrying vessels at a rate equivalent to $1 per barrel in cryptocurrency. Israel struck over 100 Hezbollah targets in Lebanon in the hours following the ceasefire, killing hundreds, prompting Iran to warn of repercussions and dispute the White House and Israel's position that Lebanon was not covered by the agreement. President Trump posted late Wednesday threatening 'bigger, and better' military strikes against Iran if a deal is not reached or complied with, while also telling Netanyahu to scale back the Lebanon strikes; Trump told NBC News on Thursday he was 'very optimistic' about a permanent peace deal. Vice President JD Vance is set to lead a U.S. delegation in talks this weekend, while U.S. troops remain deployed in the region pending Iranian compliance. Markets reflected ongoing uncertainty — oil prices rebounded Thursday before trimming gains, European and African crude hit record levels, the national average gas price reached $4.17 per gallon, and Federal Reserve officials said the conflict raised the odds of a rate cut. House Republicans blocked a Democratic resolution to limit Trump's Iran war powers during a pro forma session, and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte publicly acknowledged that allies were slow to support the U.S., while discussing potential NATO involvement around the Strait of Hormuz.

President Trump posted a warning to Iran on Truth Social on Thursday, accusing Iran of doing a 'very poor job' of allowing oil through the Strait of Hormuz and stating Iran was not living up to their agreement. A two-week US-Iran ceasefire was in place, but Iran continued to maintain significant control over Strait of Hormuz traffic, through which one-fifth of the world's seaborne oil passes. The national average price for regular gas stood at $4.153 per gallon on Friday per AAA, marking the first one-cent decrease since the ceasefire announcement, after prices had risen since February. The war with Iran was identified as a key factor driving an expected surge in U.S. consumer inflation in March 2026, with higher fuel costs also raising food and travel prices. Inside Congress, calls for investigations into prediction market platform Polymarket increased after anonymous traders made well-timed bets on major geopolitical events, including the Iran war, hours before those events occurred.

President Trump publicly condemned Iran's plans to charge fees to oil-carrying vessels traversing the Strait of Hormuz, one day after Trump himself had proposed a 'joint venture' involving similar tolls. A European airport trade body warned that if the Strait of Hormuz did not reopen within three weeks, the EU airline industry could face fuel shortages. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that U.S. inflation rose to 3.3% year-over-year in March — the highest level in nearly two years — driven primarily by a large monthly surge in gasoline prices, with the Iran war cited as the key geopolitical factor behind rising energy costs. Consumer prices rose 0.9% month-over-month in March, and consumer sentiment fell to record lows in April, also attributed to the Iran conflict.

According to NBC News, the U.S. and Iran are closing in on a preliminary agreement that would extend a ceasefire for 60 days, begin negotiations on Iran's nuclear program, and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. However, Trump administration officials subsequently walked back reports that a memorandum of understanding had been reached, according to CBS News. Pakistan's Foreign Minister is set to meet with Secretary of State Rubio in Washington to discuss Iran. Former national security adviser Jake Sullivan, while critical of the administration's approach, acknowledged the tentative deal 'may be the best of the very bad outcomes.'

Trump stated that Iran has agreed not to pursue nuclear weapons, according to Newsmax. U.S. officials reported that Trump sent tougher terms to Iran for a peace framework, with one official suggesting the changes may be intended to pressure Iran into accepting the existing deal more quickly. Saudi Arabian shares gained while Qatar's market slipped amid ongoing uncertainty over a potential deal.

President Trump stated that Iran really wants to make a deal with the United States, and urged political critics to 'just sit back and relax,' claiming critical remarks hamper negotiation efforts.
